title: Fireflies.ai: the 'AI' that was two founders typing, now worth $1 billion
disclosure: AFFILIATE LINK IN DESCRIPTION - AI VOICE

scenes.label: CLIENT CALL
scenes.narration: A client call. A silent guest named Fred joins. Fred is supposed to be an AI note-taker. But Fred is really two broke founders, typing every word by hand.

title: FRED
WAS HUMAN
scenes.subtitle: FIREFLIES.AI
scenes.narration: That startup is Fireflies.ai. Today it says it is worth over one billion dollars. This is how a human "robot" became real AI.

scenes.label: DAY ONE
scenes.narration: Fireflies starts in 2016, founded by Krish Ramineni and Sam Udotong. Their first idea is big: use AI to summarize your emails, chats and support tickets.

scenes.label: PIVOT AFTER PIVOT
scenes.narration: It does not take off. So they pivot, again and again. Different reports count five to seven pivots before something finally sticks.

scenes.label: THE REAL PAIN
scenes.narration: The idea that sticks is meetings. Everyone hates taking notes, and after the call nobody remembers who promised what.

scenes.label: FIRST CUSTOMERS
scenes.narration: So they sell an AI meeting note-taker for about one hundred dollars a month. There is just one problem. The AI is not ready yet.
So the founders join the calls themselves, as a silent guest called Fred from Fireflies. They type the notes by hand and send them minutes later. They say early clients knew a human was helping.

scenes.label: LATE NIGHTS
scenes.narration: They do this for more than one hundred meetings, living on pizza. The founders later said it paid just enough for the rent.

scenes.label: THE BIG QUESTION
scenes.narration: Was it fake? The founders say early clients knew it was human-assisted AI testing. Critics later raised privacy questions. Either way, it taught them the product.

scenes.label: BUILDING FRED
scenes.narration: Every meeting they typed showed them what people really needed. In 2017 they automated it, and Fred became real software.

scenes.label: TEAM
scenes.narration: Investors notice. Khosla Ventures and Canaan back them early, and the small team starts to grow.

scenes.label: SERIES A
scenes.narration: In May 2021, Fireflies raises a reported fourteen million dollar Series A, led by Khosla Ventures. Remote work is booming, and every call needs notes.

scenes.label: NO MORE FUNDRAISING
scenes.narration: Then something rare in AI happens. Fireflies stops raising money. The company says it has been profitable since 2023.

scenes.label: UNICORN
scenes.narration: June 2025. After a share sale for its employees, Fireflies says it is valued at over one billion dollars, with no new venture money since 2021.
The company says more than twenty million people in over five hundred thousand organizations use it, including three out of four Fortune 500 companies.

scenes.label: HOW TO USE IT
scenes.caption: FREE PLAN
scenes.narration: So how can you use it? Fireflies has a free plan. You invite its AI note-taker to your Zoom, Google Meet or Teams call, and it transcribes the conversation.

scenes.label: AFTER THE CALL
scenes.narration: After the call you get a searchable transcript and a summary. The free plan has storage limits. And always tell people you are recording.
